subject: maths
chapter_title: Predicting What Comes Next: Exploring Sequences and Progressions

concepts.title: Explicit Rule for a Sequence
concepts.definition: One rule that jumps straight to any term of a sequence from its position number alone.
concepts.key_idea: No climbing through earlier terms: plug in the position, read the term.
question_patterns: A sequence runs 4, 7, 10, ...; write its rule and find the 50th term.
If a sequence follows u_n = 2n - 1, what is u_53?
Compute the term at position 12 for the rule u_n = 5n + 3.
Which rule jumps straight to any term? State it for 6, 11, 16, ...
Evaluate the 100th term of the sequence with rule 7n - 4.

solution_steps.action: multiply index by linear coefficient
solution_steps.explain: scale position index n by linear factor

solution_steps.action: add constant offset
solution_steps.explain: add constant value to complete term evaluation

solution_steps.action: Verify the term matches the sequence pattern
solution_steps.explain: Check that the computed term is consistent with the known terms of the sequence.

concepts.title: Term Position from a Linear Rule
concepts.definition: Given a term's value and the sequence's rule, run the rule backwards to find which position holds it.
concepts.key_idea: Solve for the position instead of the term.
question_patterns: Which term of the sequence 5n - 2 equals 308?
In the sequence with rule 3n + 1, find the position of the term 91.
The term value is 100 for rule 4n - 8; calculate its position.
Locate where 149 sits in the sequence u_n = 6n - 1.
For u_n = 9n - 5, find n when the term is 220.

solution_steps.action: subtract constant offset from term value
solution_steps.explain: isolate term product by removing constant offset

solution_steps.action: divide by linear coefficient
solution_steps.explain: divide difference by coefficient to find term index n

solution_steps.action: Verify that n is a positive integer
solution_steps.explain: A valid position must be a whole number greater than zero, confirming the term belongs to the sequence.

concepts.title: Next Term from a Recurrence
concepts.definition: Build each new term out of the one before it by repeating the same operation.
concepts.key_idea: Each step needs the previous value; the recurrence is the engine.
question_patterns: The rule is multiply by 2 and subtract 1; find the next term after 15.
Each term is the previous one times 3, plus 2; continue from 5.
Apply the rule next = 2 x current - 1 to the current term 31.
A recurrence halves the term and adds 4; what follows 20?
Generate the term after 11 for the rule times 2 plus 3.

solution_steps.action: multiply previous term by constant factor
solution_steps.explain: apply multiplication multiplier to previous term

solution_steps.action: add constant addend
solution_steps.explain: add shift addend to obtain current term

solution_steps.action: Verify the next term follows the recurrence pattern
solution_steps.explain: Check that applying the recurrence rule again produces a consistent sequence, confirming the calculation is correct.

concepts.title: nth Term of an Arithmetic Progression
concepts.definition: Terms that step up or down by one fixed amount form an AP; the nth term equals the first term plus n minus 1 steps of that amount.
question_patterns: Find the 20th term of the AP with first term 3 and common difference 5.
An AP starts at 100 and steps by -7; calculate its 15th term.
What is the 9th term of the progression 2, 9, 16, ...?
For first term 4 and common difference 11, compute term 25.
State the nth term rule for the AP 12, 19, 26, ...

solution_steps.action: calculate position offset
solution_steps.explain: subtract 1 from term position n

solution_steps.action: multiply offset by common difference
solution_steps.explain: scale difference by offset count

solution_steps.action: add initial term
solution_steps.explain: add first term a to obtain nth term value

concepts.title: Finding Common Difference and First Term of an AP
concepts.definition: Subtract any term from the one right after it; that gap is the fixed step size.
concepts.key_idea: One subtraction reveals the step; it must repeat everywhere.
question_patterns: Find the common difference of the AP 7, 12, 17, ...
Calculate d for the progression 50, 43, 36, ...
What is the step size between the terms 19 and 31 in an AP?
Determine the common difference from consecutive terms 2.5 and 4.
Check whether 3, 7, 11 keeps a constant step and state it.

solution_steps.action: subtract first term from second term
solution_steps.explain: compute consecutive term difference to get common difference

solution_steps.action: Check the difference repeats between another pair of consecutive terms
solution_steps.explain: Confirming the same gap appears elsewhere verifies the sequence is truly arithmetic.

solution_steps.action: Use the common difference to find the first term if needed
solution_steps.explain: Subtract the common difference from the first known term to recover the starting value of the AP.

concepts.title: Term Position in an Arithmetic Progression
concepts.definition: Given a value sitting inside an AP, work out its position by counting how many steps of size d separate it from the first term.
concepts.key_idea: Steps taken plus one is the position.
question_patterns: Which term of the AP 3, 8, 13, ... is 78?
Find the position of 100 in the progression with first term 4 and difference 6.
Calculate the term number of 51 in the AP 7, 12, 17, ...
The value 0 appears where in the progression 21, 14, 7, ...?
Locate the term 125 in the AP with first term 5 and difference 12.

solution_steps.action: find total change from initial term
solution_steps.explain: subtract initial term a from target term value

solution_steps.action: divide total change by common difference
solution_steps.explain: determine number of step increments

solution_steps.action: add 1 to get index n
solution_steps.explain: shift step count by 1 to get term position

concepts.title: Sum of First n Natural Numbers
concepts.definition: Add the whole numbers from 1 through n by pairing ends: each pair shares one total, which gives the closed form.
question_patterns: Find the sum of the first 10 counting numbers.
Calculate 1 + 2 + ... + 100.
What is the total of the integers from 1 through 250?
Compute the closed-form total for n = 75.
Add up the first 19 positive integers.

solution_steps.action: add 1 to n
solution_steps.explain: compute next consecutive integer factor

solution_steps.action: multiply n by next integer
solution_steps.explain: multiply count by successor

solution_steps.action: divide product by 2
solution_steps.explain: halve product to evaluate total sum

concepts.title: Sum of Natural Numbers in a Range
concepts.definition: To total a run of integers from one value through another, take the up-to totals and subtract the part before the start.
question_patterns: Find the sum of the integers from 20 through 50.
Calculate the total of all counting numbers from 1 through 60.
What is the sum of the integers 31 through 99?
Compute the running total from 15 to 45.
Add the integers from 101 through 200.

solution_steps.action: calculate total sum up to end_num
solution_steps.explain: evaluate S_end for integers up to end boundary

solution_steps.action: find prior count index
solution_steps.explain: subtract 1 from start limit

solution_steps.action: calculate total sum up to prev_num
solution_steps.explain: evaluate S_start for integers prior to lower boundary

solution_steps.action: subtract lower prefix sum from upper prefix sum
solution_steps.explain: obtain net sum of interval range

concepts.title: nth Term of a Geometric Progression
concepts.definition: Terms that scale by one fixed multiplier form a GP; the nth term is the first term times the multiplier raised to n minus 1.
concepts.key_idea: First term times the ratio, repeated n minus 1 times.
question_patterns: Find the 6th term of the GP with first term 3 and ratio 2.
Calculate term 5 of the progression 81, 54, 36, ...
The first term is 5 and the ratio is 3; what is the 4th term?
For the GP 8, -16, 32, ..., find the 7th term.
State the nth term rule of the GP with first term 10 and ratio one half.

solution_steps.action: calculate exponent power
solution_steps.explain: subtract 1 from term index n

solution_steps.action: raise common ratio to power
solution_steps.explain: exponentiate common ratio r by power index

solution_steps.action: multiply by first term
solution_steps.explain: scale base value by ratio factor

concepts.title: Common Ratio of a Geometric Progression
concepts.definition: Divide any term by the one right before it; that quotient is the fixed multiplier.
concepts.key_idea: One division reveals the ratio; it must repeat everywhere.
question_patterns: Find the common ratio of the GP 5, 15, 45, ...
Calculate r for the progression 16, 8, 4, ...
What is the multiplier between successive terms 2 and -10?
Determine the ratio from consecutive terms 27 and 18.
Check whether 4, 6, 9 keeps a constant quotient and state it.

solution_steps.action: divide second term by first term
solution_steps.explain: compute ratio of consecutive terms

solution_steps.action: Check the ratio repeats between another pair of consecutive terms
solution_steps.explain: Confirming the same quotient appears elsewhere verifies the sequence is truly geometric.

solution_steps.action: Express the ratio in simplified fractional or decimal form
solution_steps.explain: Simplifying the ratio makes it easier to use in further GP calculations.

concepts.title: Bounce Height Sequences
concepts.definition: A rebounding ball climbs to the same fraction of its previous height every time; the heights shrink by repeated scaling.
concepts.key_idea: Each bounce multiplies the height by one fraction.
question_patterns: A ball dropped from 24 ft rebounds to three quarters of the height; find the height after 3 bounces.
Calculate the rebound height on bounce 2 for a drop of 12 m with rebound fraction 0.5.
What height does the ball reach on bounce 4 if it drops from 16 ft and rebounds by half?
Compute the height after 3 bounces for a drop of 45 cm and fraction two thirds.
State the rebound rule with drop height H and fraction f.

solution_steps.action: calculate multiplier power for n bounces
solution_steps.explain: raise restitution fraction to power n

solution_steps.action: multiply initial height by decay factor
solution_steps.explain: scale starting height to obtain target bounce height

solution_steps.action: Verify the height decreases as bounce count increases
solution_steps.explain: Since the fraction is less than 1, each successive bounce height must be smaller than the previous, confirming the decay is correct.

concepts.title: Geometric Progression in Fractal Patterns
concepts.definition: Self-similar shapes split into a fixed number of copies at every stage; counts grow by powers of that number.
concepts.key_idea: The stage number becomes the exponent of the copy count.
question_patterns: A triangle splits into 3 copies each stage; find the count at stage 5.
Calculate the number of pieces at stage 4 when each shape yields 4 copies.
What is the element count at stage 6 for a 2-copy split?
Determine the piece total at level 3 for a fractal that multiplies by 5 each level.
Compute the shape total at stage 7 for a 3-copy split.

solution_steps.action: raise base multiplier to stage power
solution_steps.explain: compute exponentiation of branching factor to stage index

solution_steps.action: Verify the count grows consistently with the self-similar pattern
solution_steps.explain: Each stage multiplies the previous count by the base, so the result should be base_count times the count at stage n minus 1.

solution_steps.action: Confirm the count is a positive integer
solution_steps.explain: Fractal piece counts must be whole positive numbers, confirming the exponentiation was applied correctly.

questions: Find the first five terms of the sequence in which the nth term is given by (i) tn = 3n - 4, (ii) tn = 2 - 5n, and (iii) tn = n^2 - 2n + 3 for n >= 1.

Determine whether 97 and 172 are terms of the sequence tn = 5n - 3 for n >= 1.
Which term of the sequence tn = 5n - 3 for n >= 1 is 607?
A sequence is given by the recursive rule t1 = -5, tn+1 = tn + 3 for n >= 1. Find the first five terms of the sequence. Is 52 a term of this sequence? If so, which term is it?
Let T1 = 1, T2 = 2, T3 = 4, and Tn = Tn-1 + Tn-2 + Tn-3 for n >= 4. Find T4, T5, T6, T7, and T8.
Find the 10th and 26th terms of the AP: 3, 8, 13, 18, ....
Which term of the AP: 21, 18, 15, ... is -81? Also, is 0 a term of this AP? Give reasons for your answer.
Find the nth term of the AP: 11, 8, 5, 2 ... Write the recursive rule for this AP.
An AP consists of 50 terms in which the 3rd term is 12 and the last term is 106. Find the 29th term.
How many 2-digit numbers are divisible by 3? What is the sum of all these 2-digit numbers?
Harish started work at an annual salary of Rs 5,00,000 and received an increment of Rs 20,000 each year. After how many years did his income reach Rs 7,00,000?
A child arranges marbles in rows so that the first row has 1 marble, the second has 2 marbles, the third has 3, and so on up to 25 rows. How many marbles does the child use in all?
Find the 12th term of a GP with common ratio 2, whose 8th term is 192.
Find the 10th and nth terms of the GP: 5, 25, 125, ... .
A sequence is given by the recursive rule t1 = 2, tn+1 = 3tn - 2 for n >= 1. Which term of the sequence is 730?
Which term of the GP: 2, 6, 18, ... is 4374? Write the explicit formula as well as the recursive formula for the nth term.

A ball is dropped from a height of 80 metres. After hitting the ground, it bounces back to 60% of the height from which it fell. It continues bouncing in this way - each time rising to 60% of the previous height. (i) What height does the ball reach after the 5th bounce? (ii) What is the total vertical distance the ball has travelled by the time it hits the ground for the 6th time?
Which term of the sequence 2, 2*sqrt(2), 4, ... is 128?

For the Sierpinski square carpet: (i) How many red squares are there in Stages 0 to 3? (ii) Can you predict the number of red squares in Stages 4 and 5? (iii) Can you find a rule for the number of red squares at the nth stage? Write explicit and recursive formulas. (iv) If area at Stage 0 is 1 square unit, find area of red region at Stages 1 to 5 and write explicit and recursive rules.
Find the 31st term of an AP whose 11th term is 38 and 16th term is 73.
Determine the AP whose third term is 16 and whose 7th term exceeds the 5th term by 12.
How many three-digit numbers are divisible by 7?
How many multiples of 4 lie between 10 and 250?
Find a GP for which the sum of the first two terms is -4 and the fifth term is 4 times the third term.
Find all possible ways of expressing 100 as the sum of consecutive natural numbers.
The number of bacteria in a certain culture doubles every hour. If there were 30 bacteria present originally, how many will be present at the end of the 2nd hour, 4th hour and nth hour?
The sum of the 4th and 8th terms of an AP is 24 and the sum of the 6th and 10th terms is 44. Find the first three terms of the AP.
Find the smallest value of n such that the sum of the first n natural numbers is greater than 1,000.
Which term of the GP: 2, 8, 32, ... is 131072?
The sum of the first three terms of a GP is 13/12 and their product is -1. Find the common ratio and the terms.
If the 4th, 10th and 16th terms of a GP are x, y and z respectively, prove that x, y, z are in GP.
The sum of the first three terms of a geometric progression is 26, and the sum of their squares is 364. Find the terms of the GP.
Suppose P1 = 1, P2 = 2 and for n > 2, Pn = P1 + P2 + ... + Pn-1 + 1. Find P1 through P8.
Suppose W1 = 1, W2 = 2 and for n > 2, Wn = W1 + W2 + ... + Wn-2 + 2. Find W1 through W8.
